title: Watchmen: The End is Nigh
provenance: Reported by udance4ever (highball-db#941, 2026-11-03), Apple M1, macOS 27.2, Highball 0.10.24, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r29, D3DMetal, rated 1 of 5 after 4 minutes: DirectX installs, then MultiLauncher.exe says the .NET Framework must be enabled in Windows Features, with the dotnet48 recipe installed. Not verified by the maintainer. udance4ever offered on highball-db#941 (2026-11-03) to install .NET 3.5 with winetricks' dotnet35 verb, tried on 2026-11-25 (below). udance4ever again (highball-db#941, 2026-11-25): highball tricks with dotnet35 stopped at winetricks' 'Cannot find cabextract' on the Wine 10 engine r31, also with Homebrew's cabextract installed. The CLI gives winetricks a PATH of the engine's and the system's folders only, and finds the app's cabextract only when the code runs inside the app or HIGHBALL_TOOLS points to it, which a CLI built from the repository doesn't do on its own.
notes: Doesn't start in one report on an M1. Its MultiLauncher.exe asks for the .NET Framework to be enabled, though .NET 4.8 is installed in the environment. It's a 32-bit game.

knownIssues.symptom: MultiLauncher.exe says the .NET Framework must be enabled from Windows Features, with .NET 4.8 installed
knownIssues.cause: not diagnosed. PCGamingWiki says the game needs .NET Framework 3.5, which .NET 4.8 doesn't provide, so the launcher most likely wants 3.5 (inferred, not checked here)
knownIssues.fix: none in Highball yet. Winetricks has a dotnet35 verb, untested with this game. The CLI's 'highball tricks' runs winetricks verbs, but a CLI built from the repository doesn't find the app's cabextract, which dotnet35 needs, and stops there (highball-db#941, 2026-11-25). Setting HIGHBALL_TOOLS to the app's Contents/Resources/tools folder should hand it over, not tried yet
